harness: Charm Crush (charmbracelet/crush) - Go TUI coding agent CLI
surfaces: CLI TUI (bubbletea/lipgloss) in a terminal; optional local HTTP server mode (crush serve / client-server) that streams an event API; no IDE extension, no Windows GUI app. Unix-socket state reporting exists (herdr) but is Linux/macOS-only and requires HERDR_ENV=1, so it is not usable on Windows.
binaries: crush (crush.exe on Windows). Install: winget charmbracelet.crush, scoop install crush, brew install charmbracelet/tap/crush, npm install -g @charmland/crush, go install github.com/charmbracelet/crush@latest (README L30-L176). No separate agent daemon; 'crush serve' runs an optional local server.

paths: <PROJECT>\.crush\crush.db - THE session/message store (default data dir is '.crush' inside the project)
%USERPROFILE%\.config\crush\crush.json and %USERPROFILE%\.config\crush\crushrc - global CONFIG only, no activity
storage.format: SQLite 3 (plain, unencrypted, WAL) - one DB per project at <dataDir>/crush.db with tables sessions, messages, files, read_files, mcp_enabled, mcp_disabled, stats. Message payloads are JSON blobs in messages.parts. Secondary append-only slog JSON log at <dataDir>/logs/crush.log (operational only, no tool calls). NO JSONL session log exists anywhere upstream: grep for 'jsonl' over the full source tree = 0 matches.
storage.append_semantics: Rows are written live during the run: the assistant message row is created when the model starts a turn, tool_call parts are flushed on a 33ms debounce tick (defaultUpdateDebounce, message.go L16-21), tool_result parts on completion, and a finish part closes the turn. But the container is a SQLite file in WAL mode, so bytes land in crush.db-wal and are checkpointed into crush.db later - a byte-offset line tailer is meaningless; a consumer must re-query the DB.
storage.session_file_naming: No per-session files. sessions.id is a UUIDv4 string (session.go L104), parent_session_id links sub-agent sessions, and all sessions/messages live in the single per-project crush.db. Project grouping = data dir; the sessions table has no cwd column.

fields.project: yes - project root comes from %LOCALAPPDATA%\crush\projects.json entry 'path' (or the parent of data_dir); sessions table itself stores no cwd
fields.model: yes - messages.model (provider model id, e.g. 'claude-sonnet-4-5') plus messages.provider (e.g. 'anthropic') (migration 20250627000000_add_provider_to_messages)
fields.file_basename: yes - tool_call part 'input' JSON carries file_path (view/edit/write/multi_edit/download/lsp_*) or path (ls/grep/glob)
fields.tool_activity: yes - tool_call part {id,name,input,provider_executed,finished} and tool_result part {tool_call_id,name,content,is_error} (message/content.go L110-128); tool names: view, edit, write, multi_edit, bash, ls, grep, glob, fetch, web_search, download, todos, question, ...; the files and read_files tables additionally track edited/read paths
fields.phase: yes (derived) - user message = turn start; reasoning part = thinking; tool_call/tool_result = running tools; finish part (reason stop/canceled/error) = turn end; session 'todos' column / todos tool = planning
fields.timestamps: yes - messages.created_at/updated_at, sessions.created_at/updated_at and read_files.read_at are Unix SECONDS (strftime('%s','now')); reasoning parts carry started_at/finished_at in Unix seconds; ordering is by created_at (1-second resolution, ties are common) then row order

parser_strategy: Not line-based. parse_line_for(Provider::Crush, _) must return Vec::new() (never feed the binary DB to the text tailer). Instead add a new function, e.g. events::parse_crush_rows(rows, project_path) -> Vec<ParsedEvent>, fed by a DB poller: read-only SQLite connection (URI 'file:<db>?mode=ro', busy_timeout ~2s), SELECT id, session_id, role, parts, model, provider, created_at FROM messages ORDER BY created_at, rowid, filtered by a per-DB watermark (last seen updated_at / message id set) so only new rows are decoded. Row mapping: role='user' -> ParsedEvent::TaskStarted{started_at_ms: created_at*1000}; role='assistant' with non-empty model/provider -> ParsedEvent::AgentDetected{agent: "<model> (<provider>)"} after a sanitizer identical in spirit to deepseek_model_label (ASCII alnum plus -_.:/@ , length cap, reject prose/newlines); parts: type 'tool_call' -> ParsedEvent::TrackedToolStarted{call_id: data.id, activity: ToolActivity{label: classify_tool(name, command), file: basename(input.file_path|input.path), language: language_from_file(basename)}}; type 'tool_result' -> TrackedToolFinished{call_id: data.tool_call_id}; type 'reasoning' -> Thinking{reasoning: None} (never the thinking text); type 'finish' -> Completed; type 'text' -> ignored entirely; before the first row of a session emit SessionMetadata{project: last path component of the project path, cwd: project path}. The tool_call 'input' is a JSON string that must be parsed and then narrowed to file_path/path/command only - old_string, new_string, content, description and prompt are dropped on the spot. classify_tool already covers crush's names: view->'Reading project files', edit/write/multi_edit->'Editing files', bash->'Running command' plus cargo/npm sub-labels, grep/glob->'Searching project', ls->'Reading project files', fetch/web_search->'Browsing documentation', download->'Editing files', todos->'Planning changes', question->'Waiting for input'.
discodex_plan: VARIANT: Provider::Crush, display_name 'Charm Crush'. LOGO: https://stuff.charm.sh/crush/charm-crush.png (verified HTTP 200, image/png, 791,976 bytes - the official 'Charm Crush Logo' linked from upstream README L4; @lobehub/icons-static-png@1.97.0 has NO crush asset - crush.png and crush-color.png both return 404 - and the Charm org avatar is a parent-company icon, so do not use it). from_executable: 'crush' (after .exe strip) -> Some(Provider::Crush). from_window: match 'crush' only as a whole trailing/leading token (title_ends_or_is / title_starts_or_is) - never a bare contains('crush') because of false positives such as 'Sugar Crush'; a Windows Terminal tab for the TUI is typically titled 'crush' or 'crush - <dir>'. default_activity: 'Working with coding agent'. has_session_tracking(): true only if the DB work below is accepted; otherwise keep Crush out of that list and rely on focused-app detection. SESSION SOURCES: the current SessionSource{provider,root} model (roots under dirs::home_dir()) does not fit - Crush stores its DB inside the user's project directories, not under a home root. Two additions are needed: (a) a registry root - dirs::data_local_dir().join('crush') (data_local_dir gives %LOCALAPPDATA% on Windows and $XDG_DATA_HOME|~/.local/share on Unix, which is exactly where upstream writes projects.json); (b) dynamic per-project sources discovered by parsing <registry>/projects.json (JSON array of {path, data_dir, last_accessed}) - each data_dir (e.g. C:\Users\PC\Documents\MyApp\.crush) yields a DB source with db_path = data_dir\crush.db and project root = entry.path. The registry file must be re-read when it changes (watch it NonRecursive) and on a slow timer, because new projects appear over time. is_session_log: add a new branch - filename equals 'crush.db' (case-insensitive); explicitly reject 'crush.db-wal', 'crush.db-shm', 'crush.json' and 'logs\crush.log' (SQLite sidecars and config/log files are not the store). WATCHER/MAIN CHANGES (the extra machinery): (1) New dependency: a SQLite reader. Recommended rusqlite with the 'bundled' feature (compiles the SQLite amalgamation via cc; needs MSVC; ~+1-2 min build, ~+2-3 MB binary) or sqlx-sqlite (heavier). This is a genuine new native build step for a Windows GUI release - flag the cost. (2) LogTailer cannot be reused: it is byte-offset based and the DB is a WAL file. Add a CrushSource{data_dir, db_path, project_path} list plus a poller that every ~500-1000 ms opens the DB read-only (never read-write, never run migrations, never checkpoint or delete -wal files) and re-queries rows newer than its watermark. (3) Do not rely on notify alone: in WAL mode the new bytes live in crush.db-wal, so watch the data dir NonRecursive for crush.db and crush.db-wal and treat notifications as a 'poll now' hint, keeping the periodic poll as the source of truth. (4) main.rs worker loop: add a branch next to the existing tailer.read_new()/apply_lines() path - for Crush sources call crush_poll(source) and feed each ParsedEvent into activity.apply(db_path, Provider::Crush, event, now_ms). Use the DB path as the ActivityState key (one crush.db == one project; TrackedToolStarted/Finished call_ids are unique so the tracked-tools map still works). (5) Startup: replace the historical-line scan with a crush equivalent - read the newest ~50 messages of the most recently updated session per DB, emit them, but only keep the session active if its updated_at is within the existing staleness window (mirror main.rs's 900 s cutoff). (6) Dedup: parts of a message row can be updated in place, so dedupe by (session_id, tool_call_id) for tools and by (message id, updated_at) for rows, otherwise a re-read of an updated row would replay tool events. (7) reader must tolerate SQLITE_BUSY/locked/corrupt: skip the tick, retry, and after N consecutive failures mark the source unhealthy and stop publishing Crush presence (the existing discard_stale_active() then clears the stuck presence). UNIT TESTS TO ADD: (a) privacy - a parts blob with a tool_call 'view' (input containing an absolute path) plus a text part 'PRIVATE PROMPT' and a tool_result 'SECRET OUTPUT' must yield TrackedToolStarted{label:'Reading project files', file:Some('provider.rs'), language:Some('Rust')} and TrackedToolFinished, and the serialized events must contain neither 'PRIVATE' nor 'SECRET' nor the absolute path nor any command string; (b) bash classification - tool_call name 'bash', input {"command":"cargo test -- --nocapture"} -> label 'Running Rust tests' and the raw command must not appear in the event payload; (c) row mapping - a user row (created_at 1789189713) -> TaskStarted{1789189713000}, an assistant row with tool_call id 'call_01' -> TrackedToolStarted, a row with tool_result tool_call_id 'call_01' -> TrackedToolFinished, a row with a finish part -> Completed; (d) model sanitization - model 'claude-sonnet-4-5' + provider 'anthropic' -> AgentDetected{'claude-sonnet-4-5 (anthropic)'}, while a model string containing prose/newlines yields no AgentDetected; (e) matcher/registry - is_session_log(Provider::Crush,'crush.db') is true while 'crush.db-wal','crush.db-shm','crush.json' are false, and a projects.json entry {"path":"C:\\Users\\PC\\Documents\\MyApp","data_dir":"C:\\Users\\PC\\Documents\\MyApp\\.crush"} resolves to project 'MyApp' (folder name only, never the full path). CHURN RISK AND FAIL-SAFE: upstream PR #3581 (open) would store messages.parts as zstd-compressed BLOBs (reads sniff the zstd magic 28 B5 2F FD) - the parser must detect that magic and either decompress or skip the row; never guess a file or label from an undecodable blob. Goose migrations keep adding columns (todos, channel, provider, prism_*, is_summary_message, read_files) and the parts JSON shape can change - SELECT only the stable columns, and if the query fails (column drift, new schema) disable that source and fall back to the focused-app presence instead of crashing or spamming Discord. The DB location is user-configurable (option data-directory, --data-dir), so never hardcode '<project>/.crush/crush.db' - always resolve through projects.json. Unknown part types are dropped, never echoed. If a part cannot be decoded for N consecutive polls, mark the source unhealthy and stop publishing.

risks: Wrong assumption in the brief: %USERPROFILE%\.local\share\crush is the Unix path; on Windows the global dir is %LOCALAPPDATA%\crush and it holds only crush.json + projects.json. The session store is <project>\.crush\crush.db (SQLite), never JSONL - a JSONL adapter would be a wrong path.

New native dependency: rusqlite with 'bundled' (or sqlx-sqlite) means compiling SQLite C in the Windows release pipeline - build time, toolchain (MSVC), and binary size must be accepted before starting this adapter.

Ingestion is not a file tail: the DB lives in user project folders, is written in WAL mode (crush.db-wal), and is a live SQLite file. Requires a poller + read-only open + project discovery through projects.json - a fundamentally different adapter shape from Codex/DSH/Antigravity.

Format churn: upstream PR #3581 would zstd-compress messages.parts; goose migrations keep adding columns (todos, channel, provider, prism_*, is_summary_message, read_files); part JSON shapes evolve. Fail-safe: sniff zstd magic, SELECT only stable columns, drop unknown part types, and disable the source (falling back to focused-app presence) on repeated decode/query failures.

Event fidelity: 1-second timestamp resolution, in-place part updates, and rows that can be rewritten after being read mean a naive row scan can duplicate or skip tool events. Must dedupe by (session_id, tool_call_id) and (message id, updated_at) and use a watermark.

Privacy: tool_call 'input' contains the full command, old_string/new_string, and file content; tool_result 'content' holds raw output. The parser must narrow to file_path/path/command and a fixed label, and never serialize a parts blob into the Discord payload.
One crush.db == one project, so presence is per project rather than per session, and sub-agent sessions (parent_session_id) collapse into the same project entry.

Project discovery depends on projects.json, which is only written when crush starts in client mode (root.go L315); a project started with a custom --data-dir is still registered, but a DB copied in from elsewhere would not be.
Window-title detection for 'crush' risks false positives (e.g. 'Sugar Crush'); match only whole tokens.

Upstream may add the requested export format (issue #1965); if a JSON/JSONL session export lands, the cheaper tail-based adapter becomes viable - keep the design modular so a second, tail-based source can be added later.
confidence: High for layout, format and field recoverability: read directly from upstream main @ 2ec8c1e (internal/db/*, internal/config/*, internal/message/*, internal/cmd/root.go) and corroborated by upstream issue #1965 quoting the real path '.crush/crush.db (SQLite)'. Medium for live-timing nuances (1-second timestamp resolution, in-place part updates, 33ms flush debounce) and for the projects.json-only discovery path, since the data dir is user-overridable. Logo URL verified by HTTP HEAD (200, image/png).
summary: Charm Crush stores everything locally, but in SQLite, not JSONL: one plain (unencrypted) SQLite DB per project at <project>/.crush/crush.db (Windows: C:\Users\PC\<Project>\.crush\crush.db), with sessions/messages/files/read_files tables; message payloads are JSON blobs in messages.parts containing tool_call / tool_result / reasoning / finish parts, plus model, provider and Unix-second timestamps. Rows are written live (33 ms flush debounce) in WAL mode, so project, model, current file basename, normalized tool activity, phase and elapsed timer are all recoverable without shipping any conversation text. The only append-only text file (<dataDir>\logs\crush.log) is operational and contains no tool activity; there is no JSONL anywhere upstream. On Windows the global dir is %LOCALAPPDATA%\crush (not %USERPROFILE%\.local\share\crush, which is the Unix path) and holds only crush.json plus a projects.json registry that maps project path -> data_dir. Verdict: rich, but this is a structurally different adapter - it needs a SQLite reader (new dependency, native build), per-project discovery via projects.json instead of a home-dir root, and a poller instead of the existing append-only LogTailer.
